_comment: AS 5100.2:2017 road and rail traffic load models.
THESE NUMBERS ARE THE LEAST RELIABLE IN THE ENTIRE PACKAGE.
Everywhere else in austruct a [VECTOR] tag marks a single coefficient
that needs checking. Here it marks the GEOMETRY AND MAGNITUDE OF AN
ENTIRE LOAD MODEL. If an axle spacing or an axle load is wrong, every
bridge number the toolkit produces is wrong, and plausibly so.
The values below are the author's best recollection of AS 5100.2
Sections 6 and 9 and their figures. They have NOT been transcribed from
the printed standard. Before this file is used for anything:
1. Open AS 5100.2:2017 Section 6 (road) and Section 9 (rail), and the
M1600 / S1600 / A160 / W80 / HLP / 300LA figures.
2. Confirm or correct every axle offset, every axle load, the UDL
intensities, the wheel contact areas and spacings, and the minimum
spacing between axle groups.
3. Set status to VERIFIED and record checked_by and checked_on.
Confidence, worst first -- check in this order:
HLP320/HLP400  the author is NOT confident of the axle count, the
axle load or the group arrangement. Treat as a
placeholder that shows the shape of the data only.
300LA          configuration recalled, not transcribed. The rail DLA
is span-dependent and is NOT implemented at all.
M1600/S1600    axle group arrangement recalled; the number of groups
is fixed here but the standard varies it to suit the
span.
A160/W80       simplest, and most likely to be right, but still
unchecked.
ADDING A LOADING
Every model follows the same schema, so a new one -- an ARTC rail
loading, a state authority vehicle, a project-specific crane -- is a
data edit here, not a code change. Copy the nearest entry and adjust.
SCHEMA
kind          'road' or 'rail'
geometry.type 'axles' for an explicit list, 'groups' for repeated
axle groups at a variable gap
axles         [[offset_mm, axle_load_kN], ...] measured rearwards
from the front of the vehicle
udl           lane/track distributed load, kN/m, applied over the
loaded length behind the vehicle
wheel         contact geometry PER WHEEL. n_per_axle wheels spaced
`spacing` apart transversely; contact_length is along
the direction of travel, contact_width across it
dla           dynamic load allowance as a FRACTION (0.35 = 35%), or
null where it is not a constant
source: AS 5100.2:2017 Section 6 (road traffic) and Section 9 (rail traffic)

W80.description: Individual heavy wheel load. Governs local effects -- deck slabs, and the top of a buried structure under shallow fill.

A160.description: Single axle load. Governs short spans and local effects.

M1600.description: Moving traffic load. The general design vehicle for global effects.
M1600._note: CONFIRM n_groups -- the standard varies the number of groups to suit the span rather than fixing it at two.

S1600.description: Stationary traffic load. Governs where traffic queues; carries no dynamic allowance.

HLP320.description: Heavy load platform, 320 tonne. Checked only where the road authority nominates an HLP route.
HLP320.confidence: PLACEHOLDER -- axle count, axle load and group arrangement are NOT trusted
HLP320._note: The author is not confident of any figure in this entry. It is present so the catalogue has the slot and the schema is visible. Transcribe the real configuration from AS 5100.2 before use.

HLP400.confidence: PLACEHOLDER -- axle count, axle load and group arrangement are NOT trusted

300LA.description: Railway traffic load, 300LA. Axle groups of 300 kN with a 100 kN/m distributed load.
_note: The rail dynamic load allowance is NOT a constant -- AS 5100.2
Section 9 makes it a function of the loaded length. dla is null
here and with_dla() refuses rather than applying a wrong number.
The nLA designation scales with the axle load: 250LA is 300LA with
250 kN axles. Use scaled_la(250) rather than adding an entry.

lane_factors._note: Accompanying lane factors. First loaded lane 1.0, subsequent lanes reduced.
